common_name: Michael Pastel Hybrid Lady's Slipper Orchid

planting.note: Set dormant, lab-propagated crowns shallowly in fall into cool, humus-rich woodland soil in dappled shade and leave undisturbed.

directions: This German Frosch-line hybrid crosses the Chinese species Cypripedium henryi with Cypripedium macranthos, producing a compact plant topped with pure white pouches backed by ivory sepals in late spring above pleated, lance-shaped leaves. Like other hardy lady's slippers it relies on a root-zone mycorrhizal partner, so plants should come from tissue-culture labs rather than wild collection or amateur seed-starting. Give it a cool, evenly moist woodland bed with leaf-mold-rich soil and dappled shade, and expect several seasons before a single crown bulks into a multi-stemmed clump. Keep it away from summer heat pockets, since both parent species favor cooler mountain conditions.

common_name: Sabine Pastel Hybrid Lady's Slipper Orchid

planting.note: Plant lab-grown crowns shallowly in fall in humus-rich, well-drained woodland soil; this selection tolerates more summer heat than most Cypripedium.

directions: Bred from the Chinese species Cypripedium fasciolatum and Cypripedium macranthos, this named selection is a rare clear white-flowered form of the standard 'Sabine' grex, opening its pouches in early spring on stems that top out around a foot and a half. Nurseries that have grown it since the mid-2000s note it handles heat and humidity noticeably better than many Cypripedium, making it a realistic candidate for warmer temperate gardens rather than strictly alpine ones. Plant divisions in a shaded, leaf-litter-mulched bed with steady moisture and sharp drainage, and avoid disturbing the crown once it is settled. It is sold as a seed-grown, flowering-size plant through specialty mail-order woodland nurseries.

common_name: Philipp Dark Hybrid Lady's Slipper Orchid

planting.note: Set bare-root crowns shallowly in fall in cool, humus-rich woodland soil; this selection builds into a notably robust clump over time.

directions: A darker-flowered sister selection to the well-known 'Philipp' grex, this hybrid of the American Cypripedium kentuckiense and the Chinese Cypripedium macranthos produces large, deep raspberry pouches framed by purple sepals streaked with white. It is among the tallest and most vigorous of the Frosch breeding line, forming a substantial multi-stemmed clump nearing two feet given several growing seasons in favorable conditions. Plant lab-propagated crowns in a cool, consistently moist woodland bed with rich leaf-mold soil and part-sun to light shade, and mulch every autumn to protect the shallow roots. Specialty growers report it performs unusually well through hot, humid summers for a Cypripedium hybrid.

common_name: Lucy Pinkepank Hybrid Lady's Slipper Orchid

planting.note: Plant nursery-grown crowns shallowly in fall into gritty, humus-rich soil in dappled shade; this cross is noted for exceptional garden vigor.

directions: Registered in 1998, this hybrid pairs the robust American species Cypripedium kentuckiense with the brightly colored Chinese species Cypripedium tibeticum, yielding large fuchsia-red streaked pouches in early spring on sturdy stems. It is regarded among lady's-slipper enthusiasts as one of the more forgiving hybrids for garden culture, establishing and multiplying faster than many straight species crosses. Site it in a humus-rich, evenly moist woodland bed with dappled light, and resist any temptation to divide or move the crown once it settles in. Source only tissue-culture-propagated plants from specialty orchid or woodland perennial nurseries.

planting.note: Plant lab-grown crowns shallowly in fall in cool, humus-rich woodland soil in light shade.

directions: Raised in 2005 by British orchid breeder Peter Corkhill, this compact hybrid combines the North American Cypripedium parviflorum var. pubescens with the Chinese species Cypripedium fasciolatum to produce soft cream pouches backed by light brown sepals each spring. It stays smaller than many Frosch-line crosses, making it a good fit for tighter shaded borders or raised woodland beds where space is limited. Grow it in humus-rich, well-drained but consistently moist soil under light shade, mulching lightly each fall to protect the shallow root system from freeze-thaw heaving. As with all hardy lady's slippers, buy only laboratory-propagated stock and leave established plants undisturbed.

common_name: Queen of the Mist Hybrid Lady's Slipper Orchid

planting.note: Plant lab-propagated crowns shallowly in fall into cool, humus-rich soil in dappled shade.

directions: Cypripedium ×ventricosum occurs naturally where the ranges of the European Cypripedium calceolus and the Asian Cypripedium macranthos overlap, and 'Frosch's Queen of the Mist' is a named selection of that cross propagated through the German Frosch breeding and tissue-culture program. It produces softly blended pouch flowers in spring that combine traits of both parent species, on compact stems suited to smaller shaded beds. Grow it exactly as you would a species Cypripedium: cool, humus-rich, evenly moist woodland soil, dappled shade, and a permanent planting site that is never disturbed once the crown is established. Because it depends on a specific mycorrhizal fungus to thrive, only plant nursery stock raised with that fungal partner already present.

planting.note: Plant lab-grown crowns shallowly in fall in humus-rich, cool woodland soil in dappled shade.

directions: Bred by Werner Frosch from the European Cypripedium calceolus and the Chinese Cypripedium shanxiense, 'Schoko' takes its name from its medium-sized, lightly fragrant flowers with pendent cinnamon-brown pouches rimmed in yellow, backed by matching cinnamon sepals. Its fragrance is a distinctive trait among Cypripedium hybrids and makes it a good candidate for a shaded path edge where passersby can catch the scent. Plant it in cool, humus-rich, consistently moist soil in part sun to light shade, and leave the crown permanently in place once it is sited, as with all hardy lady's slippers. Buy only laboratory-propagated plants from reputable specialty growers rather than attempting to raise it from seed.

common_name: Mother Earth Hybrid Lady's Slipper Orchid

planting.note: Plant this clonal selection's lab-grown crowns shallowly in fall in cool, humus-rich woodland soil in light shade.

directions: This is a named clonal selection taken from the 'Inge' seed strain, itself a cross between the North American Cypripedium parviflorum var. parviflorum and the Chinese Cypripedium fasciolatum, chosen for an especially large, long-lasting creamy pouch set off by amber-purple, mustache-like sepals. Blooming in mid-spring, it reaches a respectable mid-size among Cypripedium hybrids and holds its flowers longer than many relatives, extending the display in a shaded border. Grow it in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil under part sun to light shade, mulching with leaf litter each autumn to insulate the shallow rhizome. Because it is propagated clonally from a single outstanding plant rather than from mixed seedlings, expect more uniform flower quality than from an unselected seed strain.
